name: Vercel
summary: Managed frontend cloud with Git-based deploys, preview URLs, serverless and edge functions.
use_cases: Deploying Next.js and other frontend frameworks with preview environments per pull request.
tradeoffs: Not suited to long-running processes or persistent WebSocket servers.
Costs can rise with bandwidth and function usage.
avoid_if: you need long-lived servers or must self-host.

name: Fly.io
summary: Platform that runs your Docker images as lightweight VMs (Machines) close to users in many regions.
use_cases: Full-stack apps and WebSocket servers that need multi-region deployment without managing Kubernetes.
tradeoffs: More infrastructure concepts (machines, volumes, regions) than frontend-only hosts.

name: Cloudflare Workers
summary: Serverless functions running on Cloudflare's edge network, with Durable Objects for stateful coordination.
use_cases: Low-latency APIs, edge middleware, realtime coordination with Durable Objects.
licence: proprietary (managed service); workerd runtime is Apache-2.0
tradeoffs: Runtime is not full Node.js; some packages need compatibility flags or alternatives.
avoid_if: you rely on native Node modules or long CPU-bound tasks.

name: Docker Engine
summary: Container runtime and tooling for packaging applications and their dependencies into portable images.
use_cases: Reproducible builds, self-hosting services on a VM, local development environments.
tradeoffs: You run and patch the host yourself.
Docker Desktop has paid licensing for larger companies (Engine on Linux does not).
avoid_if: you want a fully managed platform with no servers.

name: Kubernetes
summary: CNCF container orchestration platform for deploying, scaling and managing containerised workloads.
use_cases: Many services with autoscaling needs, platform teams, portable deployments across clouds.
tradeoffs: High operational and cognitive overhead for small teams.
avoid_if: you are a small team running a handful of services.

name: Coolify
summary: Open-source, self-hostable platform-as-a-service for deploying apps, databases and services on your own servers.
use_cases: Heroku/Vercel-style Git deploys on your own VPS, keeping control of infrastructure and costs.
tradeoffs: You are responsible for the servers, backups and uptime.

name: Render
summary: Managed cloud for web services, background workers, cron jobs, static sites and managed Postgres.
use_cases: Small teams deploying full-stack apps with workers and a database without managing servers.
tradeoffs: Fewer regions and less low-level control than hyperscalers.
